title: Lethal force justified, review found
article: Travis Douglas Oakes had no intention of giving up to police when boxed in at a southwest car wash about 3 a.m. on March 18, 2009, a fatality inquiry into his shooting death heard on Friday.

In a report filed by officer safety unit Sgt. Gerard Forde of the Edmonton police, Calgary police's High Enforcement Auto Theft supervisor Sgt. Dave Jennings was found to have been justified in using lethal force to prevent Oakes from fleeing in a stolen Chevrolet Caprice and endangering not only police officers involved in the arrest, but members of the public.

"Oakes' mindset during this incident can only be speculated," Forde wrote in his report. "However, indications from the ASIRT (Alberta Serious In- cident Response Team) report show that when notified by investigators of Oakes' death, a witness advised that Oakes told (the witness) that he would not go back to jail, as it was too hard on him. The witness also, reportedly, advised CPS investigators that Oakes would not have stopped for the police officers and that Oakes had advised (the witness) of a previous chase with the police."

Forde, being questioned about the report by Calgary Police Service lawyer John Cordeau, concluded the actions and tactical decision-making in the incident that followed a six-hour surveillance were considered to be appropriate and reasonable.

Forde told the inquiry he based his conclusions on the fact that Jennings fired only after Oakes' response to officers identifying themselves and telling him to give up, and twice rammed each of the covert police vehicles parked at either end of the bay of Western Pride Car Wash.

"Sgt. Jennings' initial three-round volley appeared to have little influence on Oakes," Forde wrote in his report. "His fourth and final shot resulted in a noticeable decreased acceleration of the Caprice and ultimately facilitated an end to the confrontation."

Forde said, overall, the situation was a result of the suspect's actions as he failed to follow verbal commands issued by the officers inside the neighbouring bay of the car wash and immediately responded by repeatedly ramming the unmarked police vehicles that had cornered him.

"The officers present, both inside and outside the wash bay, found reasonable and probable grounds to believe that Oakes intended to escape, regardless of the threat it posed to the officers involved and ultimately to the community at large."
